item.title: Neighborhood Swap Day
item.description: Practise vocabulary for sorting and labeling items at a neighborhood swap day. Talk about what to exchange, what to save for someone, and what to donate at the end.

children.definition: To put things into groups according to their type, size, or another feature.
children.example: We sorted the children's clothes by size before putting them on the tables.

children.definition: To write information on something or attach a tag to it to show what it is or give details about it.
children.example: Nina labeled each box with the age range of the toys inside.

children.definition: To give someone one thing and receive another thing from them in return.
children.example: I swapped my puzzle for a bag of building blocks.

children.definition: To keep something for a particular person or purpose so it will be available later.
children.example: Could you set aside that winter coat for Amir until he gets here?

children.definition: A place where people leave items to be gathered together.
children.example: The volunteers set up a collection point for spare school supplies near the entrance.
collocations: bring items to the collection point

children.definition: Still there after the rest has been used or taken.
children.example: We packed the leftover books into two boxes after everyone had gone home.

children.definition: To let someone use something for a while with the expectation that they will return it.
children.example: Could you lend us a folding table for the afternoon?

children.definition: The state of an object, especially how much it is worn or damaged.
children.example: The lamp still works and is in good condition.

children.definition: To take something to a place and leave it there.
children.example: Maya dropped off a bag of shoes at the welcome table on her way to work.
children.translation_ru: приносить или привозить и оставлять в нужном месте
collocations: drop something off at the entrance

children.definition: To go somewhere to collect something and take it with you.
children.example: Leo came back with his bike trailer to pick up the chair.
collocations: pick something up on the way home

children.definition: A group of things placed on top of one another.
children.example: I found a wool scarf at the bottom of the pile.

children.definition: To fix something that is broken or damaged.
children.example: Sam repaired the broken zipper before bringing the backpack to the swap.
The owner of the guitar case opened it to show me the soft lining.

children.definition: Not wanted or needed by the person who has it.
children.example: We brought some unwanted mugs that had been in our cupboard for years.
